tasks.title: A man at table 4 says his oat latte is 'aggressively beige' and wants the manager.

outcomes.text: You compliment his scarf. He tips C$5 and asks for you by name next time.
He's immune to charm. He leaves a one-star review about your 'energy.'
Odette handles it in 30 seconds. 'Next time, try first,' she says, kindly.
You remake it. It's exactly the same. He calls it 'transformative.'

tasks.title: Bashir is slammed: twelve tables and a birthday. Your section is quiet.

outcomes.text: You run his tables. Bashir hugs you in the walk-in. 'Brother.'
Your section sparkles. Bashir notices you watching. He notices.

tasks.title: Odette wants the new C$9 'deconstructed croissant' pushed hard today.

outcomes.text: You sell 22. Odette writes your name on the whiteboard with a star.
You push so hard a table leaves. Odette: 'Less... intensity.'
Three people ask. One loves it. The regulars trust you more than the menu.

tasks.title: You catch Kendall taking a twenty from the shared tip jar.

outcomes.text: Odette has a quiet word. Kendall glares at you through every shift.
'It was a loan.' Kendall puts it back and, weirdly, respects you.
You say nothing. The tip jar is lighter all week.

tasks.title: Saturday rush: forty drink orders and the ice machine is dying.

outcomes.text: You line up the orders like a pit crew. Odette films it for training.
Fast and messy. Two mojitos become one very strong mojito. Nobody complains.
You drop a tray of six glasses. The room claps. Not kindly.

tasks.title: A food critic is in, pretending not to be. Everybody knows. Kendall wants the table.

options.label: Take the table yourself
options.get: A shot at a rave review

outcomes.text: The critic writes 'service with the warmth of a sitcom family.' Odette frames it.
You overdo it. The review calls the service 'clingy.'
Kendall nails it and, shockingly, thanks you in front of everyone.

tasks.title: You're writing next week's schedule. Bashir wants Friday off; so does Kendall. Only one can.

outcomes.text: Bashir goes to his cousin's wedding. Kendall goes to HR, about nothing.
Kendall's thrilled. Bashir says 'it's fine' in the voice that means it isn't.
You cover Friday. Both of them bring you pastries Monday.

tasks.title: The demo is at 2. The login button logs people out. Dana is 'not panicking.'

outcomes.text: You find it: a missing 'not'. The demo works. Dana nods once. Huge.
You fix it and break the signup page. The demo is mostly vibes.
No button, no bug. Skyler calls it 'minimalist.'
An investor asks how to log in. Silence.
Mateo spots it in a minute. 'You owe me a bagel.' Done by 1:30.

tasks.title: At the 10am stand-up, Dana asks who has 'a big idea.' You have a medium one.

outcomes.text: You call it 'AI for laundry.' Skyler hears it through the wall. It's on the roadmap now.
Brent asks three follow-up questions you can't answer.
'Still exploring.' Dana writes something down. It isn't praise.

tasks.title: Brent's code review lands on your desk. It's bad. Like, hardcoded-passwords bad.

outcomes.text: You flag it gently. Brent fixes it and pretends he meant to.

options.label: Flag it in the team channel
options.get: Dana sees your eye for detail

outcomes.text: Dana thanks you in the channel. Brent reacts with a single thumbs-up. Cold.
Approved. Nothing happens. Yet.
The passwords leak in a week. Your name is on the approval.

tasks.title: Dana messages at 9 PM: 'quick thing.' It is never a quick thing.

outcomes.text: Two hours later it's fixed. Dana replies 'ty'. Two letters. Worth it?
'Fine.' Dana fixes it herself and mentions it in stand-up.

tasks.title: Skyler announces a pivot: Pivotly is now 'a vibe marketplace.' Your team has to explain it to users.

outcomes.text: Your post makes the pivot sound almost sane. Skyler retweets it with 🚀.
Users read it and ask for refunds. Skyler blames 'the copy.'
You say it out loud: users don't want vibes. Dana agrees, quietly, later.
Skyler calls you 'a legacy thinker.' Ouch.

tasks.title: You're on a hiring panel. Mateo's friend applied. Brent's candidate is better on paper.

outcomes.text: You go with Brent's pick. She's brilliant. Mateo understands, mostly.
Mateo's friend joins. He's... learning. Mateo buys your coffee for a month.

tasks.title: Skyler wants growth numbers up 10x by Friday. Brent suggests counting bots as users.

outcomes.text: You run three campaigns. Growth: 2.3x. Real people. Dana fights for you upstairs.
10x! Skyler rings a gong. The board is thrilled. For now.
An investor checks. Most of your users are named 'User8812'.

tasks.title: Vivian needs a headline for a story about a pigeon that rides the N train.

outcomes.text: 'YOU WON'T BELIEVE WHERE THIS PIGEON GETS OFF.' 400,000 clicks. Vivian takes credit at lunch.
'Pigeon commutes daily on N train.' 9,000 clicks. Nour loves it.

tasks.title: Vivian's coffee order is eleven words long and she hates it every time.

outcomes.text: You nail it. Vivian says 'acceptable.' The newsroom gasps.
Nour whispers: 'she wants it lukewarm.' Perfect. Nour winks.

tasks.title: A tip: Chase Clout is about to be banned again. Your source wants to stay anonymous.

outcomes.text: You run it with 'sources say.' It's right. The source sends you three more tips.
The story's airtight. Your source never answers your texts again.
Jax runs it and thanks you on air, barely. It's something.

tasks.title: Someone has to cover the overnight desk. Jax is 'feeling sick.' Jax is at a party.

outcomes.text: Quiet night until 3 AM, when a celebrity crashes a scooter into a fountain. You get it first.
Nothing happens all night. You learn every pigeon's name.
Vivian makes Jax cover the next four nights. Jax will remember.

tasks.title: You get a 90-second segment on the Big Screen. Vivian wants to 'look it over' first.

outcomes.text: Vivian 'tweaks' it. It airs as her segment, with you as 'additional reporting.'
It airs. It's great. Vivian says 'cute' and doesn't speak to you for a day.
It airs with a typo in the lower third. Vivian sighs, loudly, near you.

tasks.title: You have proof that Jax made up a quote last month. Vivian doesn't know.

options.label: Bring it to Vivian
options.get: A newsroom that tells the truth

outcomes.text: Jax is off the desk for a month. The newsroom is quiet. Vivian looks at you differently.
Jax goes pale, issues a correction and becomes suspiciously nice to you.

options.label: Leak it to Lola
options.get: A scandal with your fingerprints off it

outcomes.text: Lola runs it. Jax is done. Nobody knows it was you. Probably.
Lola names her source in a footnote, by accident. Vivian is not amused.

tasks.title: You land a sit-down with Lunaria. Her team says: no questions about the producer feud.

outcomes.text: She answers. It goes everywhere. Her team bans Clout TV. Vivian: 'worth it.'
She walks out on camera. That clip goes everywhere too, sadly.
A warm, funny interview. Lunaria's team offers you the album launch exclusive.

tasks.title: {coworker} cc'd the whole floor on your typo. With a GIF. Dana is 'reading it now.'

outcomes.text: Your 'Good catch!' gets more reactions than the GIF. {coworker} goes quiet.
You find two. Dana asks everyone to 'please stop replying-all.' Everyone blames you both.
'...Fine. Truce.' {coworker} deletes the GIF from the shared drive. Mostly.
{coworker} screenshots your DM and sends it to the group chat.

tasks.title: A customer recognizes you from the night {place} threw you out. She's telling table 6.

outcomes.text: You tell it better than she does. Table 6 tips C$20 'for the story.'
She shows table 6 the video. Odette watches it too. Twice.
Free latte, closed case. She leaves you a heart on the receipt.

tasks.title: Vivian thinks someone in the office is feeding Lola. She's looking at you. For a while.

outcomes.text: Vivian blinks first. She moves on to Kofi. Kofi has never met Lola.
The intern is 'reassigned to archives.' You feel fine about it for almost a day.
'Then you can get us an interview with her.' Vivian smiles. That's worse.

tasks.title: The Mayor is cutting a ribbon at noon. The giant scissors are missing. Marvin is 'not panicking.'

outcomes.text: Found them in the Deputy Mayor for Vibes' office, next to six other ribbons. Noon, on the dot.
You find them at 12:04. The Mayor ad-libbed for four minutes about 'the spirit of cutting.'
Tiny scissors, giant Mayor. The photo goes viral. Marvin calls it 'relatable.'
They don't cut the ribbon. The Mayor tears it with his teeth. Lola has the photo.
Dolores opens a drawer labeled 'SCISSORS, CEREMONIAL, 3 OF 3.' 'Since 1994, hon.'

tasks.title: A constituent has called 311 eleven times about the same pigeon. He's on line 2. Again.

outcomes.text: The pigeon has a name: Gerald. You promise to 'look into Gerald.' He sends a thank-you card.
Forty minutes in, he asks for your supervisor. Then your supervisor's supervisor.

options.label: Open a ticket and move on

outcomes.text: Ticket #PIG-0011 joins the queue. The queue is long and full of pigeons.
You hear Preston say 'Gerald?' through the wall. You smile.
Preston transfers him back with a note: 'He asked for you specifically.'

tasks.title: Press briefing in ten minutes. The Mayor's notes say 'say something about the potholes.' That's all.

outcomes.text: He reads them word for word, including 'PAUSE FOR APPLAUSE.' The room applauds, confused.
He ignores them and talks about his billboard for eight minutes.
'Potholes are just roads with ambition.' It's on a T-shirt by dinner.
The slogan tests badly with the Pothole Victims Association. They exist now.

options.label: Ask Marvin what to write
options.cost: Marvin takes the credit if it works

outcomes.text: Marvin dictates three lines, then tells the Mayor they were his idea. They were.

tasks.title: You found a C$40,000 line in the budget called 'Ribbon Futures.' Nobody can explain it.

outcomes.text: Marvin: 'It's for ribbons. In the future.' He closes the spreadsheet. Discussion over.
Marvin is impressed you read the budget. 'Nobody reads the budget.' You're on the next one.
You close the file. Somewhere, a ribbon is being futured.
Dolores laughs for a full minute. 'That's the Mayor's boat, hon.' You did not hear that.

tasks.title: Tonight's town hall: 40 folding chairs, 300 angry residents, one topic: the new bike lane.

outcomes.text: You raid three churches and a bingo hall. Everyone sits. Everyone still yells, but seated.
4,000 viewers. The comments are worse than the room. The Mayor reads them aloud anyway.
It trends. 'Bike Lane Town Hall' is the funniest thing in Queens this week.

options.label: Move it to a bigger room last minute

outcomes.text: Half the crowd goes to the wrong building. The meeting is calm. Too calm. Suspicious.

tasks.title: Lola has a photo of the Mayor eating a hot dog with a knife and fork. It runs at 6 unless you call.

outcomes.text: Lola agrees, 'for now.' She will absolutely collect.
Lola runs it anyway, with your quote. 'No comment, please, I'm begging.'
'Refined Papa-Dani' polls up two points. The hot dog cart guy is furious.

options.label: Have him eat one properly on camera

outcomes.text: Mustard everywhere. Real New Yorker energy. The internet forgives him.

tasks.title: A developer wants a 'quick meeting' with the Mayor. He brought a cake shaped like a condo tower.

options.label: Book the meeting
options.get: The Mayor's happy, the cake too
options.cost: The LUXURY CONDOS SOON lot gets closer

outcomes.text: The meeting goes long. The cake goes fast. A permit appears.

options.label: Decline politely
options.cost: The developer's number in your phone forever

outcomes.text: He sends the cake anyway. You eat it out of spite. It's lemon.

options.label: Log it as a gift and report it

outcomes.text: Ethics office: 'Thank you.' Marvin: 'Why.' The cake is evidence now.

tasks.title: The Mayor wants a 'Five-Borough Vibe Plan' by Friday. He hasn't said what a vibe plan is.

outcomes.text: Parks, buses, and a pothole map. The Mayor renames it 'The Papa-Dani Plan.' Of course.
Twelve slides, zero policies, one sunset photo. He loves it.
A reporter asks what slide 7 means. Nobody knows. Not even slide 7.
Top answer: 'fix the potholes.' Second: 'stop cutting ribbons.' He reads the second one twice.

tasks.title: The Mayor stops by your desk: 'Heard you're running some little campaign against me. How's that going?'

outcomes.text: He laughs too. Too long. You both keep laughing. Marvin watches from the doorway.
'Good. I like a challenge.' He leaves. Your parking permit is quietly revoked.

options.label: Offer to tell him their plans
options.cost: Your candidate, if anyone finds out

outcomes.text: He pats your shoulder: 'Loyalty. I love it.' You feel slightly disgusting.

high: You're the reason table 4 came back. Twice.
If you keep this up, I'm learning your coffee order.
Good shift. Go home before I find you more work.
mid: Fine shift. Tomorrow, smile like you mean it.
Nobody cried today. I'll take it.
The croissants are still deconstructed. So are we. See you tomorrow.
low: We need to talk about the latte foam. And the attitude.
I've seen better shifts from the espresso machine.
Take tonight to think about what 'service' means.

friend: Staff meal is lentils again. I saved you the good bowl.
Table 9 asked if we're related. I said yes. Go with it.
Same time tomorrow? I'll bring the good playlist.
rival: Cute. The regulars still ask for me.
Odette likes me more. Just so you know.
I'd tell you what you did wrong, but you'd just do it again.

high: Solid work. Don't tell Skyler, he'll give you a title.
If you're free tonight... kidding. Mostly.
mid: Fine. Let's circle back tomorrow. And the day after.
Please update your status. Your status. Your status.
low: I've added you to a 'quick sync.' It isn't quick.
Your commit messages say 'stuff'. All of them.
Let's talk about ownership. Tomorrow, 8 AM.

friend: Bagel run tomorrow? Skyler's pivoting again, we'll need carbs.
I renamed your branch 'legend'. You're welcome.
Brent asked what you're working on. I said 'synergy.'
rival: I shipped three features today. How many did you ship? Zero? Cool.
Skyler and I are 'aligned', by the way.

high: Good instincts today. I'll be using them in my segment.
You found the story before I did. Don't let it happen again.
Not bad. For an assistant. I mean that warmly.
mid: Fine. The pigeon story did numbers.
Tomorrow, find me something with a celebrity in it.
Coffee was lukewarm. Correct. Everything else, average.
low: Do you know how many people want your desk? I do. I have a list.
That was a story the way a napkin is a tablecloth.
Rethink your career. Also, my coffee.

friend: Vivian took credit for your idea again. I wrote down that it was yours.
The overnight vending machine has the good chips now. Tip.
Big Screen night tomorrow. Bring snacks, we'll heckle.
rival: I'm doing the red carpet. You're doing... the pigeon follow-up?
Vivian told me she's 'excited about my trajectory.'

high: The Mayor mentioned you. By name. Correctly. Don't let it go to your head.
Good work. I'll tell the Mayor it was my idea, as usual. You'll know.
You're on the ribbon list now. Top of it.
mid: The Mayor has thoughts. I have notes. You have both by 8 AM.
low: The Mayor asked who you were. I said 'an intern.' I was being kind.
Let's discuss your 'vision' in my office. Bring no vision.
Your memo was a text message with a header.

friend: Thirty years here, hon. The trick is: never be in the photo.
I saved you a seat in the good break room. The one with the working microwave.
Preston called the Mayor 'Dani' to his face. I almost died.
rival: My uncle golfs with the Deputy Mayor. Just saying.
I've been 'shadowing leadership.' You've been answering phones.
Cute memo. I had mine bound.
